purpose: Machine-readable evidence of source fetches (Phase 0.5 audit + Chapter 2 research + Chapter 3 research) + English Ch1-2 audit re-verification (2026-09-01)

sources.title: RDF 1.1 Primer
RDF 1.1 Concepts and Abstract Syntax
sources.key_finding: Named graph is merely syntactically paired with its graph; RDF places no formal restrictions on what the graph name denotes (provenance is an application convention, not built-in meaning). Entailment is conditional on the truth of the entailing graph.

sources.title: RDF Schema 1.1
sources.key_finding: rdfs:domain and rdfs:range are INFERENCE rules, not validation constraints. Section 3.1/3.2 confirm entailment semantics.

sources.title: RDF 1.2 Concepts and Abstract Data Model
SPARQL 1.1 Overview
SPARQL 1.1 Query Language
SPARQL 1.2 Query Language
OWL 2 Web Ontology Language Document Overview (Second Edition)
Shapes Constraint Language (SHACL)
sources.key_finding: Stable baseline for validation. Distinct from RDFS inference.

sources.title: SHACL 1.2 Core
sources.correction: Previous Phase 1 research incorrectly concluded SHACL 1.2 did not exist due to wrong URL. Correct URL is shacl12-core, not shacl-12-core.

sources.title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology
What is a Knowledge Graph?
sources.key_finding: CS520 defines KG as directed labeled graph with semantically defined labels. Minimal formal definition: subset of N x L x N.

sources.title: RDF 1.1 Turtle
sources.key_finding: Turtle is a concrete textual syntax for RDF, not the data model. Grammar is a subset of SPARQL 1.1 grammar.

sources.title: RDFLib documentation
sources.key_finding: Pure-Python RDF library: Graph/URIRef/Literal/BNode/Namespace; SPARQL 1.1 engine; many serializations. Installed version 7.6.0.

sources.title: Neo4j Data Modeling
sources.key_finding: Data modeling = define query logic and storage structure; glossary: label marks a node as member of a named/indexed subset (0+ labels per node); schema = prescribed property existence and datatypes; constraints = rules ensuring data consistency. Modeling is iterative: understand domain, draft model, test use cases, refactor.

sources.title: Neo4j Cypher Manual
sources.key_finding: elementId() returns STRING; unique among nodes and relationships across all databases in the same DBMS only within the scope of a single transaction; outside a transaction no mapping guarantees; internal IDs are reused after deletion, so applications relying on them are brittle — Neo4j recommends application-generated IDs. Old integer id() is deprecated/removed from the current manual.

sources.title: Neo4j Python Driver Manual
sources.key_finding: Driver 6.x supports Neo4j 4.4/5.x; Bolt protocol; execute_query API. Installed version 6.2.0.

sources.title: Neo4j Docker documentation
sources.key_finding: Neo4j moved to calendar versioning (2026.07 current); 5.26 is LTS. Docker tag pinned to 5.26.30-community (verified on Docker Hub).

sources.title: ISO/IEC 39075:2024 — GQL
sources.key_finding: ISO site blocks direct fetch (403); metadata cross-verified via gqlstandards.org and Neo4j GQL conformance docs.

sources.title: Neo4j Cypher — GQL conformance
sources.key_finding: Cypher accommodates most mandatory GQL features but is not identical to GQL; some mandatory features unsupported.

sources.title: GQL Standards
What Are Graph Data Models?
Knowledge Graphs (Hogan et al.), Chapter 3: Schema, Identity, Context
sources.key_finding: Schema/identity/context are three distinct extensions of the data graph; identity links (owl:sameAs) ground cross-namespace identity; context = scope of truth; reified edge does not assert the edge it reifies.

sources.title: How to Create a Knowledge Graph?
sources.key_finding: KG can start schema-less but upfront design improves usefulness; Linked Data IRI design rules; identity links use owl:sameAs; PG design = property vs label vs node, relationship properties for time-varying facts, reification for n-ary.

sources.title: How to Create a Knowledge Graph from Data?
sources.key_finding: Structured-source integration = schema mapping + record linkage; both are inexact and need human validation; mapping rules can record source provenance; reusing source identifiers is often wrong.

sources.title: OWL 2 Web Ontology Language Primer (Second Edition)
sources.key_finding: Section 4.7: OWL makes no unique-name assumption (different names may denote the same individual); owl:sameAs asserts identity and lets reasoners propagate all information between the names; owl:differentFrom required to assert distinctness.

sources.title: Defining N-ary Relations on the Semantic Web
sources.key_finding: RDF/OWL properties are binary; n-ary needs split into properties-of-a-relation (certainty, time) vs multi-participant relations; Pattern 1 introduces a class whose instances are relation instances ('reified relations').

sources.title: Wikidata Help:Statements
sources.key_finding: Statement = property-value pair about an item (Q-id); statements are contextualized with qualifiers, references, and ranks; core without references/ranks = claim; ranks (preferred/normal/deprecated) manage competing values.

sources.title: Wikidata Help:Qualifiers
sources.key_finding: Qualifiers contextualize a statement beyond the bare property-value pair: scope ('France excluding Adélie Land'), method ('population: estimation'), validity ('population as of 2011'); a statement should remain useful without its qualifiers.

sources.title: OWL 2 Web Ontology Language Structural Specification and Functional-Style Syntax (Second Edition)
sources.key_finding: Declarations are nonlogical (§5.8). Annotations have no logical effect (§10). Object vs data properties structurally distinct (§5.3-5.4).

sources.title: OWL 2 Web Ontology Language Direct Semantics (Second Edition)
sources.key_finding: Interpretation is 10-tuple with separate data domain Δ_D disjoint from object domain Δ^I. Declarations and annotations have no logical consequences. Serialization syntax ≠ semantic regime.

sources.title: OWL 2 Web Ontology Language Profiles (Second Edition)
sources.key_finding: EL PTIME only for core tasks (not conjunctive queries). QL supports query rewriting to SQL. RL on arbitrary RDF may miss answers (completeness not guaranteed). No profile is subset of another.

sources.title: Knowledge Graphs (Hogan et al.), Chapter 4: Deductive Knowledge
sources.key_finding: OWL 2 DL 'roughly corresponds to' SROIQ. TBox/ABox/RBox as formal tuple components. Decidability vs tractability explicitly distinguished. OWA/CWA contrasted.

sources.title: OWL 2 Web Ontology Language RDF-Based Semantics (Second Edition)
sources.key_finding: Gives semantics directly to RDF graphs. Annotations are NOT semantically inert under RDF-Based (unlike Direct Semantics). Serialization syntax ≠ semantic regime. Direct Semantics conclusions are subset of RDF-Based conclusions.

sources.title: RDF 1.1 Semantics
sources.key_finding: Normative model-theoretic semantics for RDF/RDFS. Section 9 defines RDFS interpretations and entailment patterns (rdfs2-domain, rdfs3-range, rdfs9-subClassOf, etc.). Appendix A shows rule-based operationalization is correct but not complete on standard RDF; completeness requires generalized RDF syntax.

sources.title: SPARQL 1.1 Entailment Regimes
sources.key_finding: Entailment regimes are specified via SPARQL Service Description (sd:defaultEntailmentRegime, sd:entailmentRegime), NOT via FROM clause. Standard regime IRIs defined for RDF, RDFS, D, OWL-Direct, OWL-RDF-Based. FROM selects graphs, not regimes.

sources.title: SWRL: A Semantic Web Rule Language Combining OWL and RuleML
sources.key_finding: Horn-clause rules extending OWL DL; undecidable in general when combined with OWL DL. Safety condition requires head variables appear in body. NOT a W3C Recommendation.

sources.title: RIF Core Dialect
sources.key_finding: Definite Horn rules without function symbols (= Datalog). Safeness conditions guarantee forward-chaining termination. First-order semantics. Stable normative reference for rule interchange.

sources.title: Knowledge Graphs (Hogan et al.), Rules and Reasoning sections
sources.key_finding: Formal rule definition R := (B,H); materialization as R*(G) = union of R^k(G); fixpoint reached when R^{k'}(G) = R^{k'+1}(G); soundness vs completeness definitions; RDFS rules correct but incomplete; OWL RL rules incomplete for negation/existentials/counting.

sources.title: OWL 2 Web Ontology Language Profiles — OWL 2 RL section
sources.key_finding: Six rule tables (Tables 4-9) covering equality, properties, classes, class axioms, datatypes, schema vocabulary. prp-dom/prp-rng demonstrate domain/range as inference rules. Theorem PR1 gives conditional completeness. Sound but not complete on arbitrary RDF.

sources.title: PROV Data Model (PROV-DM)
sources.key_finding: Conceptual provenance model underlying PROV-O. Core: Entity, Activity, Agent with relationships (wasGeneratedBy, wasDerivedFrom, etc.). Provenance forms directed graphs rooted at the entity. Generation precedes usage. Influence underlies all relations.

sources.title: Time Ontology in OWL
sources.current_revision_status: Candidate Recommendation Draft 2022-11-15 (revision in progress; not a Second Edition)
sources.key_finding: Core classes: TemporalEntity, Instant, Interval. Allen's interval algebra relations. hasTime links any resource to a TemporalEntity. Valid time vs assertion time modeled as separate temporal facts.

sources.title: R2RML: RDB to RDF Mapping Language
sources.key_finding: Triples Map translates each row of a logical table into zero or more RDF triples via Subject Map + Predicate-Object Map. Custom mapping; distinct from Direct Mapping default. Stable baseline for RDB→RDF.

sources.title: A Theory for Record Linkage (Fellegi & Sunter)
sources.document_status: Academic paper (Journal of the American Statistical Association 64(328):1183–1210)
sources.key_finding: Comparison vector gamma; m(gamma) and u(gamma) probabilities; two-threshold decision rule (match / possible / non-match with clerical review). Foundational model for record linkage / entity resolution.

sources.title: A Survey of Approaches to Automatic Schema Matching (Rahm & Bernstein)
sources.key_finding: Schema matching = identifying semantic correspondences between schema elements. Element-level vs structure-level; schema-level vs instance-level vs hybrid matchers.

sources.title: Model for Tabular Data and Metadata on the Web
sources.key_finding: Tabular data carries implicit structure (table/row/column/cell + annotations) that must be made explicit before RDF generation. Companion spec: csv2rdf (Generating RDF from Tabular Data, 2015-12-17).

sources.title: A Direct Mapping of Relational Data to RDF
sources.key_finding: Default, automatic RDB→RDF mapping: table→class, row→resource (IRI from table + primary key), column→predicate. Shape follows the DB schema, not a target ontology. Contrast with R2RML custom mapping.

sources.title: Data Integration: A Theoretical Perspective (Lenzerini)
sources.key_finding: Data integration system I = (G, S, M): global schema, source schemas, mapping. GAV/LAV mapping styles; sound / complete / exact mapping semantics. Queries posed over global schema, answered from sources.

sources.title: Knowledge Graphs (Hogan et al.), Chapter 6: Creation and Enrichment
sources.key_finding: Book Ch6 (verified via kgbook.org TOC): Creation and Enrichment — constructing KGs from data/text, entity resolution. Ch7: Quality Assessment. Academic framing; W3C standards carry formal weight.

sources.title: Knowledge Graphs (Hogan et al.), Chapter 5: Inductive Knowledge
sources.key_finding: Inductive knowledge = models encoding patterns + their predictions; generalizes from observations, fallible. Distinguishes numeric latent (KGE), numeric supervised (GNN), symbolic self-supervised (rule mining). Plausibility scoring; higher score = more plausible; training maximizes positives, minimizes negatives. High confidence != truth (capital-city 187/195 with Vaduz counterexample).

sources.title: Translating Embeddings for Modeling Multi-relational Data (Bordes et al., NIPS 2013)
sources.key_finding: TransE: relations as translations h + r ~= t; score ||h + r - t||; corrupted triples (replace head/tail) as training negatives; margin ranking loss; evaluation mean rank + hits@10 in raw AND filtered settings; known 1-to-N/N-to-1/symmetric limitations.

sources.title: Embedding Entities and Relations for Learning and Inference in Knowledge Bases (Yang et al.)
sources.key_finding: Bilinear framework: entities as vectors, relations as bilinear/linear maps; top-10 accuracy 73.2% vs 54.7% TransE on Freebase; relation composition = matrix multiplication; DistMult symmetric scoring limitation.

sources.title: Complex Embeddings for Simple Link Prediction (Trouillon et al.)
sources.key_finding: ComplEx: complex-valued embeddings, Hermitian dot product models symmetric AND antisymmetric relations; linear space/time; direct improvement over DistMult's symmetric limitation.

sources.title: Modeling Relational Data with Graph Convolutional Networks (Schlichtkrull et al.)
sources.key_finding: R-GCN: relational message passing with relation-specific transformations; encoder (R-GCN) + decoder (DistMult) for link prediction; basis/block-diagonal regularization; +29.8% on FB15k-237 over decoder-only; relation types must not be collapsed.

sources.title: Fast Rule Mining in Ontological Knowledge Bases with AMIE+ (Galarraga et al.)
sources.key_finding: Rule mining under OWA; path rules r1(x,y) ^ r2(y,z) -> r3(x,z); standard confidence penalized by incompleteness; PCA (Partial Completeness Assumption) confidence and Mostly Confident measure; KG-scale mining. Rule-mining confidence != epistemic confidence.

sources.title: Inductive Relation Prediction by Subgraph Reasoning (Teru, Denis, Hamilton)
sources.key_finding: GraIL: subgraph-based GNN for inductive relation prediction - generalizes to unseen entities without entity-specific embeddings; captures portions of first-order logic; beats rule-learning baselines on inductive benchmarks.

sources.title: A Review of Relational Machine Learning for Knowledge Graphs (Nickel et al.)
sources.key_finding: Relational ML on KGs predicts new edges; two families: latent feature models (embeddings) and observable pattern mining; combining both improves power; Knowledge Vault example links statistical models with text extraction.

sources.title: Distributed Representations of Words and Phrases and their Compositionality (Mikolov et al.)
sources.key_finding: Origin of negative sampling: training objective distinguishing observed pairs from randomly drawn negatives. A training device that assumes negatives; under OWA absence != falsity.

sources.title: Deeper Insights into Graph Convolutional Networks for Semi-Supervised Learning (Li, Han, Wu)
sources.key_finding: Graph convolution = Laplacian smoothing; stacking layers causes oversmoothing - node representations converge, performance degrades. More layers != more understanding.

sources.title: Shortcut Learning in Deep Neural Networks (Geirhos et al.)
sources.key_finding: Shortcut learning: models succeed on benchmarks using superficial/incidental cues, break under harder conditions. High benchmark accuracy can coexist with wrong mechanism understanding.

sources.title: On Calibration of Modern Neural Networks (Guo et al.)
sources.key_finding: Modern neural networks poorly calibrated / overconfident; confidence != probability of correctness; ECE; temperature scaling fixes calibration without changing accuracy.

sources.title: AI models collapse when trained on recursively generated data (Shumailov et al.)
sources.key_finding: Model collapse: training on recursively generated data causes irreversible defects - tails of the original distribution disappear; demonstrated on VAEs, GMMs, LLMs. Supports self-reinforcement caution. Reused by Ch10 for model collapse vs staleness.

sources.title: Graph Representation Learning (Hamilton)
sources.key_finding: Authoritative treatment of node embeddings (encoder-decoder), knowledge graph embeddings, GNN message passing, and graph-level pooling/readout; supports node vs subgraph representation distinction.

sources.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks (Lewis et al., NeurIPS 2020)
sources.key_finding: RAG = parametric seq2seq memory + non-parametric dense vector index; retrieval-augmented generation; query encoder + document encoder (DPR); top-k retrieved passages concatenated into prompt; RAG-Sequence vs RAG-Token.

sources.title: Dense Passage Retrieval for Open-Domain Question Answering (Karpukhin et al., EMNLP 2020)
sources.key_finding: Dense passage retrieval = dual-encoder: query encoder E_Q and passage encoder E_P; similarity = dot product; trained on in-batch negatives + BM25 hard negatives; dense retrieval outperforms BM25 for open-domain QA when trained well.

sources.title: From Local to Global: A Graph RAG Approach to Query-Focused Summarization (Edge et al., 2024)
sources.document_status: Research paper (arXiv 2024), Microsoft GraphRAG primary source
sources.key_finding: GraphRAG = LLM-built entity/relation/claim graph index from text units; Leiden community detection; bottom-up community summaries; Global Search (community summaries) vs Local Search (entity fan-out); one implementation family, not universal GraphRAG semantics.

sources.title: The Probabilistic Relevance Framework: BM25 and Beyond (Robertson & Zaragoza, Foundations and Trends in IR)
sources.document_status: Authoritative survey (Foundations and Trends in Information Retrieval 3(4), 2009)
sources.key_finding: BM25 derived from the probabilistic relevance framework (PRF); term frequency saturation (k1), document length normalization (b), inverse document frequency (idf); BM25 is a lexical/term-based ranking function, not a probability of relevance.

sources.title: Introduction to Information Retrieval (Manning, Raghavan & Schutze, Cambridge University Press 2008)
sources.key_finding: Classical IR: tokenization, inverted index, tf-idf weighting, vector space model, BM25 ranking; evaluation with precision/recall, ranked retrieval metrics; information need vs query vs document distinction.

sources.title: Cumulated gain-based evaluation of IR techniques (Jarvelin & Kekalainen, ACM TOIS 2002)
sources.key_finding: nDCG = graded relevance, position discount (log), normalized by ideal ordering; measures ranking quality with graded relevance, not binary; sensitive to graded relevance judgments.

sources.title: Reciprocal rank fusion outperforms condorcet and individual rank learning methods (Cormack, Clarke & Buettcher, SIGIR 2009)
sources.key_finding: RRF = score(d) = sum over systems 1/(k + rank_i(d)); fuses multiple ranked lists without using raw scores; rank-based fusion; produces a fused ranking for retrieval utility, not an epistemic score.

sources.title: Passage Re-ranking with BERT (Nogueira & Cho, arXiv 2019)
sources.key_finding: Two-stage retrieval: first-stage lexical retrieval (BM25) for candidate passages, then cross-encoder BERT re-ranker scoring query-passage pairs jointly; re-ranking improves MRR@10 on MS MARCO; cross-encoder compares query and passage jointly.

sources.title: Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts (Liu et al., TACL 2024)
sources.key_finding: LLMs use information at the beginning and end of long contexts more reliably than information in the middle; performance drops when relevant info is in the middle; context placement/ordering affects model performance.

sources.title: Measuring Attribution in Natural Language Generation Models (Rashkin et al., arXiv 2021/2022)
sources.key_finding: AIS criterion: generated text about the external world is attributable to identified sources if the source(s) support the claim; two-stage annotation (support detection + boundary detection); attribution to sources, distinct from factual correctness.

sources.title: Enabling Large Language Models to Generate Text with Citations (Gao, Yen, Yu & Chen, EMNLP 2023)
sources.key_finding: ALCE benchmark: citation quality (citation recall/precision), fluency, correctness; even strong models struggle with complete citation support; citation should link answer sentences to supporting passages.

sources.title: Introduction to Neural Network based Approaches for Question Answering over Knowledge Graphs (Chakraborty et al., 2019)
sources.key_finding: KGQA = question understanding + query generation + answer over KG; paradigms include semantic parsing (symbolic) vs information retrieval vs embedding-based; entity linking and relation linking are core subproblems; query over KG vs text retrieval are different mechanisms.

sources.title: Unifying Large Language Models and Knowledge Graphs: A Roadmap (Zhu et al., 2023)
sources.key_finding: Roadmap of LLM+KG: KG-enhanced LLMs (retrieval-augmented), LLM-augmented KGs (construction), synergized architectures; RAG over KG = retrieve relevant KG knowledge to ground LLM answers.

sources.title: Microsoft GraphRAG official documentation
sources.key_finding: Implementation: TextUnits -> entity/relation/claim extraction -> Leiden communities -> bottom-up summaries -> Global/Local/DRIFT/Basic search; one concrete implementation family, not a universal GraphRAG standard.

sources.title: Quality Assessment for Linked Data: A Survey (Zaveri et al., Semantic Web 2016)
sources.key_finding: Survey of LD/KG quality assessment: dimensions (accuracy, completeness, consistency, timeliness, trustworthiness...) with metrics and methods; supports the book quality-dimensions section.

sources.title: Knowledge Graph Refinement: A Survey of Approaches and Evaluation Methods (Paulheim, Semantic Web 2017)
sources.key_finding: Splits KG quality into completeness (link prediction) and correctness (error detection/repair); refinement = key maintenance operation for re-validation.

sources.title: Ontology Evolution: Not the Same as Schema Evolution (Noy & Klein, KAIS 2004)
sources.key_finding: Ontology evolution differs from DB schema evolution (instance data, shared mappings, changing domain understanding); underpins schema/ontology lifecycle sections.

sources.title: Ontology Versioning on the Semantic Web (Klein & Fensel, SWWS 2001)
sources.key_finding: Defines ontology versioning: version graphs, compatibility, difference representation; supports supersession/versioning discipline at system scale.

sources.title: Knowledge Vault: A Web-Scale Approach to Probabilistic Knowledge Fusion (Dong et al., KDD 2014)
sources.key_finding: Web-scale KB construction fusing extrinsic extractions with prior-KB predictions; operational example of maintenance-level knowledge evaluation.

sources.title: Never-Ending Learning (Mitchell et al., CACM 2018)
sources.document_status: Peer-reviewed magazine article (Communications of the ACM, 61(5), 103-115)
sources.key_finding: NELL runs continuously: extraction + candidate validation + self-monitoring; the closest deployed instance of a self-updating living knowledge system.

sources.title: A Survey on Concept Drift Adaptation (Gama et al., ACM Computing Surveys 2014)
sources.document_status: Peer-reviewed survey (ACM Computing Surveys, 46(4)), DOI verified via Crossref
sources.key_finding: Defines concept drift types (sudden/gradual/recurring) and detection; analogical basis for knowledge staleness and degradation over time.

sources.title: Learning in the Presence of Concept Drift and Hidden Contexts (Widmer & Kubat, Machine Learning 1996)
sources.document_status: Peer-reviewed paper (Machine Learning, 23, 69-101), DOI verified via Crossref
sources.key_finding: Foundational concept-drift paper; hidden context = unobservable cause of drift, motivating system self-observation.

sources.title: Hidden Technical Debt in Machine Learning Systems (Sculley et al., NIPS 2015)
sources.key_finding: ML system maintenance: feedback loops, data dependencies, debt perspective; frames the book knowledge-debt concept (adapted to epistemic domain).

sources.title: Do ImageNet Classifiers Generalize to ImageNet? (Recht et al., ICML 2019)
sources.key_finding: Newly-built test sets drop accuracy 11-14% (ImageNet): re-used benchmarks decay; benchmark score != real system quality.

sources.title: Data Cascades in High-Stakes AI (Sambasivan et al., CHI 2021)
sources.key_finding: Data cascades: compounding data-quality failures discovered post-deployment; supports knowledge-debt/contradiction-debt and structural maintenance framing.

sources.title: ISO/IEC 25012:2008 Data Quality Model (ISO SQuaRE series)
sources.key_finding: Data quality model with characteristics (accuracy, completeness, consistency, timeliness, traceability...); self-identifying standard number; ISO page 403 for automated fetch.

sources.title: ISO 8000-1:2022 Data Quality - Part 1: Overview
sources.key_finding: ISO 8000 series: data quality and data governance standards; data quality is a governed property; ISO page 403 for automated fetch (metadata via Wikipedia ISO 8000).

sources.title: Temporal Knowledge Graph Completion: A Survey (Cai et al., IJCAI 2023)
sources.document_status: Peer-reviewed conference paper (IJCAI 2023, pp. 6545-6553), abstract verified on arXiv
sources.key_finding: KGs are not static: TKGC adds timestamps to capture fact change over time; supports temporal dimension of staleness/freshness.

sources.title: Neo4j Cypher Manual — Scalar functions (elementId, id)
sources.key_finding: elementId() returns STRING; uniqueness guaranteed only within a single transaction across the DBMS; no mapping guarantees outside a transaction; internal IDs are reused after deletion (brittle apps) -> Neo4j recommends application-generated IDs; id() is Deprecated and returns INTEGER.
